findings.issue: With the switch on there is a millisecond-scale race at the exact expiry instant. A spend-only consume that wins just before expires_at can commit after recovery has already decided the approval is expired and terminalized the run. The click is then spent on a terminal run. The executor does not stop on an already_terminal heartbeat (D7, out of scope), so it could still run the approved call under an outcome_unknown receipt.
findings.evidence: CONSUME_APPROVAL_SQL checks `a.expires_at > now()` with now() at the consume transaction's start. has_pending_approval runs in READ COMMITTED, so it does not see the uncommitted consumed_at, and it evaluates `a.expires_at > now()` with the recovery transaction's later start time. The consume's renew_recovery_deadline UPDATE blocks on the obligation row lock that recovery holds, then matches no row because the obligation is no longer open or processing. The race cannot occur with the switch off, because a pending approval always spared the run. The window needs a consume starting within a few ms before expires_at and a due obligation claimed in that same window. The design does not address it and it is practically unlikely.
findings.suggested_fix: Optional hardening, or record it as an accepted risk in the S8-9 ledger addendum: add a small grace to the clause in both copies, for example `a.expires_at + interval '30 seconds' > now()`, so a consume that won at expiry always commits before recovery can treat the approval as expired. If the design owner prefers no grace, state the window explicitly in the ledger.

findings.issue: The compose comment and the approval_expiry_enabled doc say only the literal `true` turns the switch on. mp_contracts::loop_fold::switch_from trims and compares case-insensitively, so ` TRUE ` and `True` also turn it on. The claim is slightly false of the code. It is the same parser every other durable-loop switch uses, so behaviour is consistent.
findings.evidence: switch_from: `value.is_some_and(|v| v.trim().eq_ignore_ascii_case("true"))`.
findings.suggested_fix: Reword the comments to `true` (case-insensitive, trimmed) and nothing else.

findings.issue: The unit-test guard is text-level and weaker than its name suggests. It checks that the whole clause text appears somewhere in each function body, and that `.bind(approval_expiry_enabled())` appears once. It does not check that the clause sits inside the NOT EXISTS, or that the bind is the 3rd bind in claim_due_recovery (it follows `.bind(MANAGED_RECOVERY_LEASE_SECS)`) or the 2nd in has_pending_approval. One doc-comment line in approval_expiry_enabled is also over-long (about 140 characters).
findings.evidence: expiry_clause_violations uses `squash(body).contains(&expiry_clause(n))` and a bind count of 1. Only the DB tests, which are not run here, would catch a misplaced clause or a reordered bind.
findings.suggested_fix: Optionally assert the order of the binds (the position of `.bind(approval_expiry_enabled())` after `.bind(MANAGED_RECOVERY_LEASE_SECS)`) and rewrap the doc line. Not blocking.

findings.issue: RecordOrchestrationEvent now accepts, broadcasts and durably persists RunParked and RunResumed from ANY orchestration:write principal that owns the run. That includes a human owner, since authorize_operation returns Ok for every non-service caller, and any service holding the scope. No switch gates it, the principal is not restricted to service:execution-core, and nothing checks that the run is persistent and not waived or that a parked fold exists. Before this unit, prost skipped the unknown tags 24/25, so such a request got InvalidArgument ("event payload is required"). So with every switch off, a request that used to be refused now writes an events row and a run-stream frame. Nothing sends these events today, so the practical impact is nil until S8-5. But once S8-8 renders run_parked, a caller who is not the executor can forge "run parked" or "run resumed" (with any resumed_segment) onto an owner's run console and durable log, including for a waived run that can never park. Existing events have the same openness, so this follows the established pattern, but it widens the forgeable surface to the park state the design is careful about.
findings.evidence: record_orchestration_event: authorize_operation(&caller, "orchestration:write") then authorize_run_owner(..Mutate) and nothing else. persist_browser_event has new arms Some(RunParked) => ("RUN_PARKED", ..) and Some(RunResumed) => ("RUN_RESUMED", ..) with no principal, retention or switch check. auth.rs authorize_operation: `if caller.is_service() { require_service_scope } else { Ok(()) }`.
findings.suggested_fix: In record_orchestration_event, refuse RunParked and RunResumed unless the caller is the service:execution-core principal. Optionally also require that runs.retention_class is persistent and the run is not waived, or gate the two arms behind park_recovery_active() so that with switches off the RPC refuses them as before. Add a DB-free test that a human owner's RunParked is refused.

The implementer also reports two e2e_invoke_chain_test invoke_stream_stop failures. 127.0.0.1:9091/9092 are LISTENING (the dev stack), and AppState::new() hard-codes session_client to http://localhost:9091, while this rig never overrides session_client. So the environmental explanation is plausible, and this unit's gateway runtime diff is inert on those paths: the new match arms only fire for variants nothing emits, and the lists are read only by exact message match. findings.issue: `persist_browser_event` has no zero-retention or waived gate for the new RUN_PARKED and RUN_RESUMED rows. The invariant rests entirely on the executor never emitting them for such runs.
findings.evidence: `record_orchestration_event` authorizes only `orchestration:write` plus the run owner, then persists. There is no check of the run's retention class, whereas other handlers in this file call `retention_receipt::refuse_zdr_continuation`. Rows carry ids and a segment number only, so no content leaks, but the design invariant says zero-retention and waived runs never persist a park.
findings.suggested_fix: Consider refusing or skipping the persist for the two new variants when the run's retention class is not persistent. Add a DB test, or record the decision as a deliberate omission.
